_note: Digital Direction's classification, as data. THIS PACK HAS NO statement_of_account TYPE AND THAT IS THE POINT: Centracom's page 1 is titled 'Account Summary' and the word 'statement' appears twice. A statement rung above the default would misclassify it and run the wrong persona - a $20,123.80 error. The rule the pack spec settles on: a document with a payable amount and service line items is a bill, whatever its header says. If a statement type is ever needed it must require the ABSENCE of a current-charges block, not the presence of the word.

rungs.name: credit_memo_title
rungs._defect: KNOWN, PARKED. This is a bare search while the rung is named credit_memo_title - a bill that merely MENTIONS a credit memo is classified as one, which on this pack loads the wrong persona. Northstar's identical rung was fixed with title_near_top on 2026-08-06 and this one never was. Latent: 0 of 7 telecom second-samples print the wording. Fixing it is now a two-line edit to this file.

rungs.name: suspension_without_current_charges
rungs._why: Both halves required: a bill that merely warns about future disconnection is still a bill.

params.pattern: \b(current charges|new charges|subtotal current charges|current charges due)\b

tags._why: The CONSERVATIVE half of the pair. Anchor text alone cannot tell cleared from present, and guessing on a payment anchor gets Centracom exactly backwards: it prints 'Payments Received' and its prior is still 20,123.80 outstanding. refine_prior_balance_tags upgrades this to prior_balance_cleared only once the printed amounts prove it. If that hook never runs, the surviving claim is the safe one.

params.pattern: \b(previous balance|previous bill|previous statement balance|balance from last statement|previous balance due|previous total)\b

tags._defect: KNOWN, PARKED. primary_only is false, so page 3 of Windstream_041069076 - a SUPPORTING page - tags this bill via the 5-word prose fragment 'any past due Internet balance.', against a gold label of prior_balance_cleared. No word cutoff can reject a 5-word fragment; page scope can. Northstar's identical check is primary-scoped AND corroborated by a nonzero bucket. Fixing it is a one-line edit to this file.

tags._why: Makes the alias collapse auditable: Lumen prints three names for one carrier. Reads the pack's own vendor_aliases table.
tags._defect: KNOWN, PARKED. Counts alias PHRASES, so 'comcast' inside 'comcast business' counts twice and tags Comcast against its gold label. Fixing it is a one-line change in signals.distinct_printed_aliases_at_least - and note the naive fix is wrong: Lumen's three printed names share one canonical.

tags._why: A closed enumeration of the 'Kinetic Business by Windstream' insert's own marketing copy, cited to two real documents. NOT image_count: the genuine ad OCRs to a single collapsed raster (image_count 1), identical to an ordinary bill scanned the same way, while a normal native-PDF bill can carry 5 incidental logo images.

params.pattern: go kinetic business|gokineticbusiness\.com|scan the qr code|mybusiness\.gokinetic\.com|google play or the app store

claim._why: THIS PACK CLAIMS BY THE CARRIER, NOT THE BILL-TO. It is a telecom expense manager processing bills for several managed clients (CLYDE COMPANIES, City of Dublin, Choctaw Travel Mart), so there is no single recipient to guard on. What every one of its documents shares is that the sender is a known carrier - its domain by definition. The carrier list is short and stable; the client roster grows every time the business signs one.

rules._why: The primary guard. Reads the pack's own vendor_aliases, so onboarding a carrier is a table edit.

Secondary. A short line means a bill-to block, not a line-item description: an unrelated print shop's invoice claimed this pack merely by naming a managed client in `1x SIGNAGE FOR CITY OF DUBLIN PROJECT`.
rules._defect: NO REAL-DOCUMENT COVERAGE. Measured 2026-08-07: all 7 real Digital Direction documents are claimed by the carrier alias and ZERO reach this rule, so max_words is fitted to the over-claim it rejects rather than to a real bill. Kept because the pack's growth path is a bill from a carrier not yet in the alias table addressed to a client who is. The first real document through here should re-derive the cutoff.
